newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr seen mired in wide ranges near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr seen mired in wide ranges near-term.

text.p: The dollar parked in the middle of vast ranges in U.S. trade on Monday, and technical analysts said it could be weeks until the U.S. unit breaks to new highs versus the mark and yen.

"On a daily perspective, the dollar is topped out. We have to at least pause here for a while," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America. "We will trade sideways to lower for at least a week, maybe two weeks, before we break out to new highs."
Volatile trade since Friday has formed the dollar's current wide trading ranges.
After remarks from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin in late trade Friday, the dollar dropped precipitously from a 32-month high at 1.6755 marks and a 4-year high at 124.72 yen.

Then, following the conclusion of the Group of Seven (G7) summit in Berlin on Saturday, the dollar briefly bottomed at lows of 1.64 marks and 120.35 yen at the onset of Far East trade on Monday before quickly rebounding to roughly the middle of the two extremes.
Dealers said the dollar's bounce off its lows on Monday signalled a near-term dollar correction, but warned that studies point to downward pressure on the greenback.

"The dollar looks very negative on daily and weekly technical studies like momentum and stochastics studies, but you're still in the middle of a strong uptrend," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A.
"At turning points you typically get volatility and wide ranges because the market is unsure where to go from here," he added.
Chartists said the dollar will trade between 1.63 to 1.6750 marks and 120.20 to 124.70 yen. Any break above or below those extremes would flash an obvious bullish or bearish signal, they said.

In dollar/mark, analysts cited many layers of support until the main floor at 1.6320/00. In dollar/yen, initial support lies at 122.20 with major support at 120.30, which held overnight, Johnson said.
"My bias over the next two to three weeks would be to the downside with a potential break of 1.60/59 marks," Morden said.

On the upside, if the dollar can break 123.40 yen key near-term resistance, the next barrier lies at Friday's 124.70/80 yen high. Also, a close above 1.66 marks would be a bullish sign, Morden said. ((-- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677))
